biography.plain_text: Howard McGregor was an American industrialist based in Rochester, Michigan. He owned and helped run his family's National Twist Drill, a major local employer producing metal cutting tools for industry. The company was sold to Lear-Siegler in 1968. His substantial property holdings included the land that became Great Oaks Country Club.

long_biography.plain_text:
Industrialist Howard McGregor helped bring a community hospital to Rochester, Michigan, on land donated by his family. He led Crittenton's first capital campaign, drawing contributions from local schools, businesses and civic organisations. Employees of his company supported the hospital through deductions from their wages. The project extended the Detroit hospital's services to the rural Rochester community.

Education also benefited from McGregor's landholding. McGregor Elementary opened in 1961 on farmland he donated for the school. His public service included seats on the Rochester Board of Education and the Avon Township Library Board.
